clue.text: Its highly rated in the music world

definitions.text: Its highly rated in the music world

parts.words: Its highly rated in the music world
parts.note: read cryptically, 'highly rated' points to a musical term for playing in the very highest register

explanation.surface: A remark about something prized by the music industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly rated' looks like praise, but it means pitched very high: the Italian musical term for the uppermost register.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian term marks notes or a passage played in the topmost register of an instrument or voice.

clue.text: Fib about strong drink being pop

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fib goes round the drink

parts.note: a fib is a lie
mead is a strong drink of fermented honey

explanation.surface: Lying about a stiff drink being a soft one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and this citrus one is a classic example.

clue.text: Spur on in the belfry

parts.note: the belfry stands for the church tower and its spire

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer urging someone up in the tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to stimulate or encourage someone to act.

clue.text: Miss the Spanish notaries are confused

indicators.note: the letters of notaries are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: Spanish lawyers muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish' belongs to the definition: a Spanish miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish title for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Talks of back to front values

indicators.note: front puts that letter at the front of the next piece
back picks the last letter of the word to

parts.note: rates are values, as in exchange rates

explanation.surface: Discussing values turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length formally, delivering speeches.

clue.text: I'm to arbitrate pronto

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to mediate is to arbitrate between parties

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they will arbitrate quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is slang for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Look out that guy is a troglodyte

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old British schoolboy slang for look out
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A warning that this fellow is a cave-dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced KAY-vee) was a warning call in British public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a prehistoric cave-dweller.

clue.text: The rubbish in fat begins to eat figurine

indicators.note: in places the rubbish inside the fat

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
tat is rubbish or tasteless junk

indicators.note: begins picks the first letters of to and eat

explanation.surface: Junk in the dripping starts to eat away a small ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette is a small carved or cast figure.

clue.text: May defend swindle with skill

parts.note: a ramp is old British slang for a swindle or racket
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Someone who may defend a con done with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a noun: a defensive embankment is a thing that may defend.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or embankment round a fort, built to protect it.

clue.text: Camp centre practicing fun

indicators.note: the centre of the word Camp is its middle two letters

parts.note: using a skill means practising it

explanation.surface: Fun being practised at the heart of a holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun used as an adjective means entertaining, causing laughter or enjoyment.

clue.text: On that account Ethelred first went into the source of damger

indicators.note: one piece went into another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a threat is a source of danger (the clue misprints danger as damger)

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name Ethelred

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king walking first into peril, for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held misprints 'danger' as 'damger'; the reading is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning for that reason or because of it.

clue.text: Regulate the quality at encompassment

indicators.note: encompassment means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: calibre means quality or standard, as in a player of high calibre

explanation.surface: Controlling standards by surrounding something.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate an instrument is to adjust it against a standard so its readings are correct.

clue.text: Try out euro MP who is all wind

indicators.note: out marks the trial word as the outer piece

parts.note: to try is to test
E is the symbol for the euro
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Trying out a European politician who is all hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm.

clue.text: When teatimes occur as an approximation

indicators.note: the letters of teatimes occur in another order

explanation.surface: Asking roughly when teatimes happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occur' signals the letters of TEATIMES appearing in a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is a rough calculation or guess of a value.

clue.text: Hate detail from the shadow match

parts.note: de is the French and Latin for from
a test is a match, as in a cricket Test match

explanation.surface: Loathing a detail from a match played in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture. 'detail' and 'the shadow' play no clear part in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe or abhor it intensely.

clue.text: Notice god of the underworld will fail to hit man

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to miss is to fail to hit
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A deity of the dead swings and misses a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice here is warning of termination of employment, as in being given your notice.

clue.text: Bob's known for the quick way of doing things

definitions.text: Bob's known for the quick way of doing things

parts.words: Bob's known for the quick way of doing things
parts.note: a bob is a short haircut, so the phrase for quick methods also describes the hairstyle

explanation.surface: A man named Bob famous for efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a person, but it is the haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick routes or methods that save time, and also brief trims like a bob.

clue.text: Dumb actor unfinished as first musician

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the name is lost

parts.note: Harpo Marx played a mute character in the Marx Brothers films
first is written 1ST, with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A silent performer cut short becomes the leading player.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo Marx never spoke on screen; dropping his last letter gives HARP.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the stringed instrument plucked by hand is a type of musician.

clue.text: Shy time for poverty

parts.note: shy can mean short, as in two short of a dozen
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A timid era of want.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or scarcity, which poverty can mean.

clue.text: Method of cooking prison whitebait

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
whitebait are fry, tiny young fish

explanation.surface: How the jail kitchen prepares tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-frying is fast cooking in a wok over high heat.

clue.text: Euphemism the French will interrupt

parts.note: heck is a mild euphemism for hell
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A mild French curse that breaks into conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a speaker with jeers or comments.

clue.text: Greek cross at opposing wine

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X
anti means opposed

explanation.surface: An angry Greek against a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany.

clue.text: Escape from common sounding cage

parts.note: a lea is meadowland, like a village common

indicators.note: sounding means the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a cage said aloud gives the sound KAGE

explanation.surface: Breaking free of an ordinary noisy cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an escape of liquid or gas through a hole.

clue.text: Pad with a mass of hair

parts.note: a mat is a tangled mass, as of matted hair
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Padding made from a heap of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad can mean a cushioned base for sleeping on, like the stuffed bed base.

clue.text: Bet nothing will work but trouble and strife

parts.note: SP is the starting price in betting
O is zero, nothing
to use something is to work it

explanation.surface: A gamble that will fail, with only marital strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for wife, which a spouse can be.

clue.text: Tramping out with a game bird

indicators.note: out signals the letters being knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hiking outdoors with a grouse in view.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain grouse, white in winter, is shot as game.

clue.text: Is up to mythical bird, care of hot wind

indicators.note: in a down clue sense, up turns the word Is backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A legendary bird delivers a parcel care of a hot breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dusty Mediterranean wind blowing from North Africa.

clue.text: Deny what it takes to get a yes

parts.note: takes means gains, as in obtains
ay is an old or dialect form of yes

explanation.surface: Refusing what it costs to win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or dispute a claim.

clue.text: As accepting the final price for putting air in

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word As holds other letters
the final letter of the word the

parts.note: a rate is a price, as in the going rate

explanation.surface: Accepting the final charge for inflating something.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerating a liquid or soil means filling it with oxygen or gas.

clue.text: Hastens expeditions free of charge outside Eccles

indicators.note: free of means the named letters are taken out of expeditions

parts.note: ions are electrically charged particles, standing for charge

indicators.note: the outside of Eccles is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Hurrying trips at no cost beyond a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester, known for its currant cakes. Removing IONS from EXPEDITIONS leaves EXPEDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite something is to speed it up or hurry it along.
